_about: The Instagram schedule for @learn1ng.curve. The daily publishing task posts each item on its date once its media is live on thelearningcurve.net (merged to main). Times are Australia/Sydney. kind: carousel (images from public/images/curiosity/<slug>/), image (one image), reel (public/videos/curiosity/<slug>.mp4). trial: true publishes a reel as a Trial Reel (non-followers first, shared with followers automatically if it performs). status: planned (to be produced), ready (produced and in a PR or on main), published (done; add the permalink).

items.brief: Brain Glitch: the Stroop test. Viewer says the ink colour of mismatched colour words; reveal why reading wins. Source: Stroop (1935), Journal of Experimental Psychology 18(6).
Brain Glitch: why you forget what you walked into a room for. Doorways act as event boundaries. Source: Radvansky, Krawietz & Tamplin (2011), Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology 64(8).
Myth or Fact? 'I'm a visual learner.' Verdict: myth. Source: Pashler, McDaniel, Rohrer & Bjork (2008), Psychological Science in the Public Interest 9(3). Run a Story poll on the 27th first.
Brain Fact reel: about 2% of body weight, about 20% of the body's energy. Source: Raichle & Gusnard (2002), PNAS 99(16).
Can You Solve It? No. 02: the surgeon riddle (the surgeon is his mother). Schemas fill gaps. Source: Bartlett (1932), Remembering.
Memory Lab reel: the forgetting curve and why spacing beats cramming. Sources: Murre & Dros (2015) PLOS ONE; Cepeda et al. (2006) Psychological Bulletin 132(3).
Brain Glitch: change blindness. Two versions of an original scene flicker with a blank between; find the change. Source: Rensink, O'Regan & Clark (1997), Psychological Science 8(5).
Memory Lab No. 02: why you forget, and how to stop. Ebbinghaus, the 2015 replication, spacing. Sources as for the forgetting-curve reel.
Memory Lab reel: what your brain does with today's learning while you sleep (consolidation). Source: Rasch & Born (2013), Physiological Reviews 93(2).
Myth or Fact? 'We only use 10% of our brain.' Verdict: myth. Source: Beyerstein (1999), in Della Sala (Ed.), Mind Myths. Story poll on the 4th first.
